goal: Map figures part 1: valid coordinates, points mode, hexbin mode as a GeoJSON choropleth source (M1a; Board gate 180: hex cells are choropleth polygons per DESIGN.md, so the server sends centres and size, not marker data)

acceptance_criteria.text: app/geo.py view(columns, rows, typed, mapping, settings) returns {"charts": [map2d], "map3d": None} (map3d and regions come in the next Map ticket); wired into main._appview for app == "map"; primary numeric = apps.measures(...)[0] or None

valid points = rows with lat in -90..90 and lon in -180..180; points.tsv / places.csv: 20 rows give mode "points" with data lon, lat, color (primary numeric or None) and row (view row index), z_label = primary name (places.csv: pop), columns and rows holding the drawn rows as strings (at most 5000)

more than 5000 valid points (big_csv, 60,000) give mode "hex" with data lon, lat, count, size: cell size s = lon span / 40 (1.0 when the span is 0), pointy-top axial rounding as in ARCHITECTURE.md 'Round 5: Map app' (hex cell centres), sorted by (q, r); sum(count) == number of valid points and len(count) < 60000
shown = valid points, total = view rows, in both modes; the chart dict uses the existing _chart shape plus the keys above (kind "map2d")

A hex test with a hand-checkable file (three points in one cell, one in another, size fixed by the lon span) checks the counts; the unit test for points mode checks colour data equals pop and the None-colour rows
The hex test file is built inline in tests/test_geo.py (a 5,001-row file is enough: set the module constant HEX_AT via monkeypatch for the small cases)
/app for places.csv returns shown map and charts[0].kind map2d; for big_csv mode hex
Moves acceptance items AC-51, AC-52 forward
